title: Customer probe snagbook and feature threads
content:
Purpose and scope:
- Working notebook for small-scope patches and feature threads surfaced by frontline CS and a set of 12 pilot customers (enterprise + scale SaaS).
- Combine raw vignettes with quick-impact request bundles, estimate signals (freq / severity / engineering cost) and propose next-step probes.

TL;DR summary (one-paragraph):
- Two recurring friction classes: (A) per-request latency spikes when customers use long-context chat + tool-calling (notably affects canary customers running Dedicated pools), and (B) cost/accuracy trade complaints when teams try quantized models with high token churn — they want a safer rollback path and clearer docs. Quick patches: a) ephemeral KV-cache tuning knob (low-effort, high ROI for chat-heavy flows), b) a usage-visible canary mode flag that pins fallbacks and logs model variant switches (medium effort), c) docs + sample configs for quantization fallbacks (low effort).

Raw vignettes (unedited customer quotes and short threads):
- "We noticed conversation A->B suddenly doubled latency at ~t=1200 tokens; switching to smaller model fixed it but cost went up unexpectedly." — Customer Alpha (SaaS).
- "When we enabled 4-bit quant we got hallucinations in code generation paths; rollback was messy because the client didn't expect variant routing." — Beta Enterprise.
- "Need ability to surface token-level cost to end-users in our app to justify rate limit increases; current per-request cost estimate is too fuzzy." — Gamma Team.
- "Canary deploys are great, but we want an explicit 'pin fallback' so our downstream doesn't get a surprise change mid-run when the autoscaler shifts routes." — Delta Fintech.

Signal assessment (frequency / severity / current evidence):
- Latency spikes with long-context: frequency = medium-high (seen in 7 customers), severity = high (user-facing timeouts, revenue risk). Logs: traces in APM show disproportionate attention kernel time for long KV lookups; tracing links -> JIRA-INF-4212.
- Quantization regressions: frequency = low-medium, severity = medium (quality regressions in narrow domains), evidence: two reproducible evals + PR notes in serving-runtime PR #287.
- Cost transparency asks: frequency = high (many requests in CS slack), severity = low-medium, evidence: customer screenshots and billing disputes (CS-3321).

Proposed quickpatches and probes (ranked by expected ROI):
1) KV-cache aggressiveness knob (ephemeral): allow customers to set a per-route cache-ttl and a prefix-depth cutoff. Why: fixes many long-chat regressions by reducing repeated KV recompute and avoids heavy kernel ops. Est cost: 3 engineer-days to wire config + tests. Owner: Grant H. Impact: high, low infra risk.
2) Canary-pinning flag for fallbacks: API flag that tells the routing layer not to switch model variant mid-request and to log a deterministic fallback choice per-session. Est cost: 1.5 s/w + 2 infra days. Owner: Sana K. Impact: medium-high (reduces surprise regressions for Fintechs).
3) Quantization-rollback runbook + sample configs: docs + example config that automatically routes failing evals to a higher-precision variant for the same model family. Est cost: 2 doc-days + 1 eng bugfix day. Owner: Maya C. Impact: medium.
4) Token-cost debug header and sample UI snippet: return estimated token cost in response headers and a small snippet to surface to end-users. Est cost: 2 eng-days + 1 FE day. Owner: Priya S. Impact: medium.
5) Lightweight local eval harness for customer-specific prompts: small tooling to reproduce regression locally using customer prompt sets and pinned model variants. Est cost: 5 eng-days; good for supporting sales/CS escalations. Owner: Ethan R. Impact: medium-high for enterprise.

Small implementation notes / tech constraints:
- KV-cache knob: keep default conservative for hosted users; dedicated customers can opt-in via route-config. Implementation should avoid breaking continuous-batching invariants (serving runtime note).
- Canary pin: must play nicely with autoscaler; implement as routing metadata so the scheduler still makes capacity decisions but per-request routing adheres to pinned variant.
- Quantization: recommend staged rollout model: run quantized variant in parallel with a small percentage of traffic and compare eval metrics, route back if specific eval thresholds hit.

Suggested low-friction experiments to run this quarter:
- A1: Deploy KV-cache knob to 3 pilot customers (Alpha, Delta, Epsilon) for 2 weeks; track median p95 latency and token cost delta. Success metric: p95 latency drop >= 15% with < 5% token-cost increase.
- B1: Expose canary-pin flag to top-5 Dedicated customers; observe number of mid-request fallbacks avoided and customer-reported surprises. Success: reduce surprise-change incidents by 80% for participants.
- C1: Publish quantization runbook and add a client-side example; collect feedback and 3 reproduction reports. Success: reduce rollback time from reported incidents from days to hours.

Prioritization matrix (concise):
- High impact / low effort: KV-cache knob, quantization runbook, token-cost header.
- High impact / medium effort: canary-pin.
- Medium impact / medium effort: local eval harness.

Open questions and risks (notes-to-self):
- How will dedicated SLA commitments interact with aggressive KV caching that may mask upstream model issues? Need legal check and SRE input.
- Does adding token-cost headers leak sensitive pricing structure to competitors via network scans? Add ACLs or require auth.
- Can the routing metadata for canary-pinning introduce jitter in autoscaler metrics? Add simulated load tests.

Action items (next 6 weeks):
- Week 0: sync with SRE and infra on KV-cache design (Grant + SRE) — owner Grant.
- Week 1: prototype a toggle in dev cluster and smoke test with 1 internal customer (Epsilon) — owner Grant + Ethan.
- Week 2: implement canary-pin RFC and run it by Product for policy/UX — owner Sana.
- Week 3: draft quantization runbook and publish internal doc; link to sample configs in repo — owner Maya.
- Ongoing: collect customer logs and billing examples for token-cost header design — owner Priya.

Notes for CS handoff and customer messaging (short drafts):
- Messaging skeleton for customers who opt in to KV-cache knob: "We're offering a configurable chat performance knob that reduces long-conversation latency in exchange for a small, opt-in cache TTL. We'll share before/after metrics during a 14-day pilot."
- For canary-pin: "Enable pinned fallbacks to avoid mid-request model changes. This preserves consistent behavior for in-flight sessions at the cost of slightly reduced failover flexibility."

Appendix: linked evidence and quick reproductions
- Trace snippet links: confluence.redwood/internal/traces/2025-09-longchat-01 (attached).
- Repro script for quantization failure: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/quant-eval/sample-repro.md (PR #287).
- Customer support thread snippets: internal Slack thread CS-#field-ops (see JIRA-CS-3321).

Final notes (freeform):
- Keep this doc living — I expect to fold in one-pagers from Product-hosted-api and a dedicated rollout checklist.
- Prioritize low-friction changes first; these yield trust with customers and reduce noise for the larger architectural efforts.
- TODO: schedule 30-min sync with Legal on token-visibility implications.

- 2025-11-12: added KV-cache knob proposal after SRE brainstorm (Grant).
